tasks.title: A library is closing. What do its readers need to know?
tasks.summary: A neighborhood library will close for repairs. Write a short notice that helps readers plan their next visit, with the same facts available to everyone.
tasks.description:
A neighborhood library will close for repairs. Write a notice in 80 words or fewer. Make the next steps easy to find.

Closed 12–16 November. Reopens 17 November. Book returns remain open. Reservations are held. No late fees during closure.

tasks.title: What should happen when the connection drops?
tasks.summary: A reading app sometimes loses a saved note on a weak connection. Improve the save behavior using the same report and starting code.
tasks.description:
“I tapped Save. Then my note was gone.”

Reproduce: write a note, switch to a weak connection, then tap Save. Keep the draft until saving succeeds. Do not create duplicate notes. The issue report and starting code are shared inputs for this concept task.

tasks.title: How do you find your way when the usual route is closed?
tasks.summary: One entrance to a railway station is closed. Design a clear set of directions for someone visiting for the first time, including a step-free route.
tasks.description:
A station entrance is temporarily closed. The remaining entrance is on a different street. Explain the alternative route, including the step-free entrance, without assuming the visitor already knows the station.

This is a fictional wayfinding brief for the prototype, not real travel advice.

tasks.title: Can a repair guide make the first step feel possible?
tasks.summary: A small desk lamp has stopped working. Turn a technical troubleshooting note into instructions that help a beginner decide what to check and when to ask for help.
tasks.description: Rewrite a fictional troubleshooting note for a first-time reader. Make the order of checks clear and explain when to stop and seek qualified help. The task concerns the clarity of a guide, not a real repair procedure.

tasks.title: What needs to survive a meeting summary?
tasks.summary: A community meeting ends with competing priorities and a few clear decisions. Write a short summary that preserves both the decisions and the unresolved questions.
tasks.description: Create a concise summary from a fictional meeting transcript. Distinguish decisions from suggestions and unanswered questions. Do not imply agreement where the participants have not reached one.

tasks.title: How should a form help someone recover from a mistake?
tasks.summary: A long application form rejects a submission with an unclear error. Improve the feedback while preserving everything the person has already entered.
tasks.description: A fictional application form reports a validation error without identifying the relevant field. Propose behavior that helps the user locate and correct the error while retaining their existing input.

tasks.title: What can a small museum label help us notice?
tasks.summary: An everyday object is placed in a local museum. Write a brief label that gives it context without telling visitors what they should feel about it.
tasks.description: Write an interpretive label for a fictional museum object. Use the shared facts to introduce context, leave room for the visitor’s interpretation, and distinguish known facts from uncertainty.

tasks.title: How do you explain a change without losing the important details?
tasks.summary: A neighborhood event changes its time and location. Prepare a concise update that helps people understand what changed and what they need to do next.
tasks.description: Using a fictional event brief, write a clear update explaining the new time and location. Preserve the details people need in order to attend. Do not introduce information that is absent from the brief.

concept-library.title: A practical notice
concept-library.text:
Library closed for repairs: 12–16 November

We reopen on 17 November. You can still return books while we are closed. Your reservations will be held, and no late fees will be charged during the closure.

Thank you for your patience. We look forward to welcoming you back.

concept-library.title: Your next visit
concept-library.text:
Planning a visit? Please come from 17 November.

The library will be closed for repairs from 12 to 16 November. Book returns remain open, reservations are held, and there are no late fees during the closure.

concept-library.title: Dates first
concept-library.source: Illustrative agent work; no actual model run
concept-library.text:
Temporary library closure

Closed: 12–16 November
Reopening: 17 November

During repairs, book returns remain open. Reservations will be held and no late fees will apply during the closure. Please plan your next visit for 17 November or later.

concept-library.title: A brief update
concept-library.source: Illustrative agent work; no actual model run
concept-library.text:
Our library is taking a short break for repairs, from 12–16 November. We reopen on 17 November.

You can still return your books. We will hold your reservations, and no late fees will be charged during the closure.

submission.title: A library is closing. What do its readers need to know?
submission.summary: A neighbourhood library needs a clear, reassuring notice for its readers.
submission.description: The library closes from 12–16 November and reopens on 17 November. The outside book return stays open. No overdue fees accrue during the closure. Write a notice in no more than 80 words.

human.title: A small pause, a warm welcome back.
human.body:
Your library is taking a short break for repairs, 12–16 November.

You can still return books through the outside book drop, day or night. There will be no overdue fees during the closure.

We look forward to welcoming you back on 17 November.

human.title: The essentials, at a glance.
human.body:
Library closed: 12–16 November
Reopening: 17 November

The outside book return remains open. No overdue fees will be charged during the closure. Thank you for your patience while we improve your library.

agent.title: A notice for every reader.
agent.body:
Our library will be closed for repairs from 12 to 16 November, reopening on 17 November.

The outside book return will remain available throughout. No overdue fees will accrue during this period.

Thank you for your understanding. We look forward to seeing you again.

agent.title: Plan your next visit.
agent.body:
Planning a visit? The library is closed for repairs, 12–16 November. Please come back on 17 November.

Returning a book? Use the outside book drop at any time.

Worried about fees? No overdue fees accrue while we are closed.

comments.body: I would start with the practical information a reader needs next.
The two approaches make different assumptions about what is already familiar. It helps to make those assumptions visible.

Clarity matters here, but so does what gets left out. I would look for a response that preserves the constraints without making the reader work to reconstruct them. A shorter answer is not automatically a clearer one.
I found it useful to return to the original task before choosing.
The wording changes how I understand the same facts.
I am still considering which approach makes the next step easiest.
